aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is a plane in the air space between the first and second lenses, with an opening of 0.100 mm radius against a plate radius of 0.312 mm and clear semi-diameters of 0.42 mm and 0.45 mm on the surfaces beside it

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.56 nm (the d line, the wavelength the source's nd and νd refer to), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states nd and νd at the d line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single nd/νd pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

quantities.note: the engine is 4.7e-4 mm long. Two causes, both measured: the index-reference convention of the CONSTANT_INDEX material (about 0.08 %, see AIR_REFERENCED_INDEX_AS_ABSOLUTE) and the source's three-decimal rounding of f (a 3-decimal value carries +/-5e-4 mm, wider than the 6.0e-5 mm allowance). The prescription itself reproduces the source: an air-referenced build of the same numbers gives EFL 0.500017 mm
no source value: the publication states no back focal length

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: d line; the publication's TABLE 4 'f' row for Example 1, in the same millimetre units as its surface table (TABLE 1). TABLE 4 is headed 'TABLE 4' and has one column per example; the value is a specific focal length, not a normalised target (f = 1.000 would be the normalised form)

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point
nominal_back_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states no back focal length: TABLE 4 lists f, f1, f2, f3, d1-2, R2F and R2R only, and no other table in the publication states one. The value is left null rather than inferred from the prescription

aperture.note: the publication states no aperture: TABLE 1 gives radii, thicknesses and indices only, and TABLE 4 lists f, f1, f2, f3, d1-2, R2F and R2R. materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and νd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.basis: closest published glass by nd and νd in catalog 2026-11-25.1 (1226 glasses). A cross-check only: the record keeps the source's own nd as a constant index
closest published glass by nd and νd; compared, never substituted
closest published glass by nd and νd; compared, never substituted

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's νd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source's nd is an index relative to air at 20 C and 101325 Pa (the glass-catalogue convention); the Project carries it as a CONSTANT_INDEX value, which this engine reads as an absolute index and normalises by the air index at the evaluation wavelength (n_air = 1.00027716 at 587.722 nm vacuum). The modelled index relative to air is therefore nd / 1.00027716, 2.77e-4 below the source's. Measured on the engine with a single plano-convex test lens (index 1.500000, R 10 mm): EFL 20.0164 mm, not 20.0000 mm. On this prescription it accounts for the whole first-order gap: rebuilt with index_reference = AIR in the materials table, the same numbers give EFL 0.500017 mm, while the committed Project gives 0.500473 mm (0.09 % long). The batch's material convention is followed rather than corrected per record, because declaring AIR here would make this record's index convention differ from the rest of the batch

the source states no clear aperture, an F-number or a field, so no semi-diameter can be derived from a stated value. Each surface was given a clear semi-diameter that clears the axial marginal ray of the 0.100 mm stop opening by at least 3x and keeps every element's edge thickness within 150 % of its clear diameter (0.42 mm at surfaces 1-2, growing to 0.50 mm at surface 7), edged at 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture. They set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

the publication states no aperture, so the stop opening (0.100 mm radius, f/2.50 at the engine's 0.5005 mm EFL) is a layout choice, not a source value. It sets the stop plate and the solid checks only; no aperture field is recorded in the record
the source states no object distance; the Project is built for an object at infinity, which is the conjugate the stated f = 0.500 mm belongs to

the source's last row (surface 7) states no thickness, so the image distance is taken as zero and the last surface vertex is the image plane. The paraxial image falls 0.0237 mm in front of that plane, which is the source's own rounding, not a conversion choice
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the engine derives it as 0.312 mm, larger than the opening and inside the clear apertures beside it
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding, and the importer raised no warning

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states an effective focal length (0.500 mm) but no back focal length, and the format requires both. The engine's 0.500473 mm EFL and -0.023684 mm BFL are recorded under first_order.engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts

the engine's EFL is 4.7e-4 mm (0.09 %) longer than the source's 0.500 mm, which is 7.9x the format's allowance. The gap is measured, not tuned away: the index-reference convention of a constant-index material accounts for all of it (an air-referenced build of the same numbers gives 0.500017 mm, i.e. the source's value to its own three decimals), plus the source's three-decimal rounding of f
